title: GFP-RFP Plate Reader Assay
author: Sebastiaan Kuiper
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.784hryw
materials: Start plate reader protocol go to step #2

steps.title: Prepare media and autoclave
steps.instruction: Prepare M9TG medium and PBS buffer according to standard recipes and autoclave both solutions.

steps.title: Configure plate reader settings
steps.instruction: Program the BioTek Synergy MX microplate reader with the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Set temperature to 37 °C and pre‑heat before proceeding.
Set shaking to Medium speed for 0:30 (MM:SS).
OD600 read: absorbance endpoint, wavelength 600 nm, read speed Normal, delay 100 ms, 8 measurements per data point.

GFP fluorescence read: endpoint full plate, three filter sets – all with excitation 485 ± 9 nm, emission 512 ± 9 nm, optics Bottom; gains 50, 75, and 100 respectively; read speed Normal, delay 100 ms, 10 measurements per data point.

RFP fluorescence read: endpoint full plate, two filter sets – both with excitation 555 ± 9 nm, emission 585 ± 9 nm, optics Bottom; gains 100 and 150 respectively; read speed Normal, delay 100 ms, 10 measurements per data point.

steps.title: Grow overnight bacterial culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate the desired strain into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL M9TG medium and incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: After overnight growth, pellet the cells and wash twice with PBS:

substeps.instruction: Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL PBS.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension step once more.

steps.title: Load samples into 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the assay plate by adding PBS and culture to each well:

substeps.instruction: Add 160 µL PBS to each well of a clear‑bottom, black‑sided 96‑well plate.
Add 40 µL of the washed overnight culture to each test well.
For the control well, add 160 µL PBS plus 40 µL non‑fluorescent bacteria.

steps.title: Retrieve and process data
steps.instruction: Collect the plate‑reader output and perform data correction:

substeps.instruction: Retrieve raw fluorescence and OD600 data from the computer.
Normalize fluorescence values by the corresponding OD600 measurements.
Subtract the autofluorescence measured in the control sample from all experimental samples.
